analysis.title: Sales Trader Commentary: Squeezing the Shorts, Fading the Rallies; Navigating TAIEX Chaos Before Heading to the Vice City (GSTW, 12 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Taiwan's equity index rose 14% from the day low on the 11/6/2026 open, then fell more than 1,000 points on 11/12 with a last-hour fade and higher turnover. The author says he had been writing a different narrative before the fade.

Foreign sentiment is cautious. Many hedge funds were squeezed by the rally but have not covered all shorts because of the new short-sell restrictions. The market still exhausts the short-sell quota almost every day.
Hedge funds have de-grossed heavily, among the most aggressive de-grossing in GS prime book data. A more sustainable rally needs long-only funds to participate and add positions back.

Foreigners have net sold Taiwan equities for 10 straight sessions, about US$25.4bn, mostly in TSMC. TSMC saw its first foreign net buy in about two weeks on the prior day, and some real-money inflows into TSMC came this week.
Local funds were good-size net buyers that absorbed foreign outflows, mainly from retail mutual fund subscriptions.

Short interest remains high in crowded long sectors, most in ABF/CCL (NY Plastics) followed by CPO names. Smid cap outperformance was mostly short covering. Oversold names (Delta, Chroma, KYEC) drew little bottom-fishing. ASE is the author's pick for the most convicted foreign long.

Retail is described as the most important factor now. With the National Stabilization Fund boosting sentiment, many retail investors held or bought the dip, and some who faced margin calls were saved by the rally. Margin loan balance and maintenance ratio are the data to follow in coming weeks.

Fundamentals are good, with most companies reporting record quarterly earnings and monthly revenue up MoM. Investors expect AI capex growth to slow or plateau over the next 2 years. Quanta's call said 2027 growth stays high but is unlikely to match the triple-digit pace of 2026.
Author's view is that earnings outlooks probably matter less than positioning and macro backdrop. Hon Hai is the last major 3Q26 report this week.

MSCI quarterly review adds NYPCB (8046 TT) and TUC (6274 TT) and removes Lotes (3533 TT), Chailease (5871 TT), Wan Hai (2615 TT) and E-Ink (8069 TT). Kinsus (3189 TT) was not added because of its disposition status.

Risks cited: rebound was aggressive so risk-reward is unattractive, momentum is not constructive, Nvidia and Jensen headlines are unhelpful, credit risk around neocloud revenue growth, and cross-strait tension at the Trump-Xi meeting at next week's APEC Summit.
Author's view: not bearish and does not think the market is broken, but downside risk has risen. A lighter book might fare better, and Nvidia reports next week.
earnings_insights: Most Taiwan companies reported record-high quarterly earnings for 3Q26 (reported, per the author). Monthly revenue grew MoM.
Quanta (2382 TT) earnings call on 11/11 indicated still-high growth in 2027 but unlikely another triple-digit year like 2026.
Hon Hai (2317 TT) is expected to be the final major 3Q26 report this week. Nvidia is set to report next week.

macro_indicators.reading: Market expecting a rate hike in Dec'26 and Mar'27
macro_indicators.interpretation: The author says the market seems to process macro prints well with these hikes priced, so rate expectations are not the main source of equity stress right now.

risk_factors: Further unwind or volatility after an aggressive rebound with weak momentum
Nvidia and Jensen Huang headlines ahead of Nvidia's report next week
Credit risk tied to neocloud revenue growth and what it costs those companies
Cross-strait tension at the Trump-Xi meeting at the APEC Summit
Slowing or plateauing AI capex growth over the next 2 years
Retail margin calls if the market falls again
vol_and_positioning: Hedge funds have de-grossed heavily, among the most aggressive de-grossing in GS prime book data.
Short interest remains elevated in crowded long sectors, most in ABF/CCL (NY Plastics), then CPO names. Short-sell quota is exhausted almost daily under the new short-sell restrictions.
Foreigners net sold 10 straight sessions, about US$25.4bn, mostly TSMC. Local funds net bought to absorb flows.
Retail margin loan balance and maintenance ratio are the data the author is watching for signs of stress or re-leveraging.
geopolitical: Cross-strait tension may be a focus at the Trump-Xi meeting at the APEC Summit next week. A strongly negative comment on Taiwan could unsettle macro traders, such as Xi's comment just before publication.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is cleaner after the squeeze and retail held or bought the dip with National Stabilization Fund support. Fundamentals are good with record quarterly earnings, and the author is not bearish and is excited about next week.
tension_points.bear_case: Foreigners have net sold 10 straight sessions, there is little conviction to chase into year-end, and the author says risk-reward is not attractive and momentum is not constructive. Positioning is not clean enough for another 10% climb in the index.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustainable rally needs long-only funds to participate and add positions back. A rise in retail margin calls (margin loan balance and maintenance ratio) or an assertively negative comment on Taiwan at the Trump-Xi meeting at APEC would weaken it.

tension_points.bull_case: Most companies report record quarterly earnings and Quanta's call pointed to still-high growth in 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors expect AI capex growth to slow or plateau over the next 2 years, and 2027 growth is unlikely to match the triple-digit pace of 2026.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Nvidia's report next week is the next fundamental catalyst the author names, and Hon Hai's report this week closes out 3Q26 earnings.

theme_stances.key_argument: Risk-reward is not attractive after the aggressive rebound and positioning, not earnings, is driving the market.
theme_stances.evidence: Cautious optimism is perhaps the most positive thing I can say for now.

theme_stances.key_argument: Investors expect AI capex growth to slow or plateau, and Quanta's call fits that narrative.
theme_stances.evidence: People are anticipating AI capex growth to slow down or even plateau
